# Mental Health & Music

Assumptions: Self reported study data may not be fully representative of the population and may have un-measured variables leading to unknown bias in the data

```{r load unit packages, echo=FALSE, message=FALSE, warning=FALSE, results='hide'}
library(tidyverse)
library(lmtest)
library(sandwich)
library(patchwork)
library(testthat)
library(ca)
library(dplyr)
library(stargazer)
library(ggrepel)
library(factoextra)
library(cluster)
library(RColorBrewer)
library(here)

theme_set(theme_minimal())
options(stargazer.header = FALSE)
knitr::opts_knit$set(root.dir = here::here())
```

## Splitting The Data

```{r}
# Set seed for reproducibility
set.seed(42)

# Randomly assign each row to exploration (1) or confirmation (2)
# 30% exploration = 1, 70% confirmation = 2
my_data_int <- my_data %>%
  mutate(
    UsedForTesting = sample(
      c(1, 0),
      size = n(),
      replace = TRUE,
      prob = c(0.30, 0.70)
    )
  )

# Verify the split
table(my_data_int$UsedForTesting)
prop.table(table(my_data_int$UsedForTesting))
```

### Creating the split for Testing & Validation

#### Testing Data Set (Exploration - 30%)

```{r}
my_data_testing <- my_data_int %>%
  filter(UsedForTesting == 1)

# Verify
nrow(my_data_testing)
```

#### Validation Data Set (Confirmation - 70%)

```{r}
my_data_validation <- my_data_int %>%
  filter(UsedForTesting == 0)
```

#### Saving The Testing and Validation File To Workspace

```{r}
write.csv(my_data_testing, "data/my_data_testing.csv", row.names = FALSE)

write.csv(my_data_validation, "data/my_data_validation.csv", row.names = FALSE)

```

## Principle Component Analysis

```{r}
# Select the 4 mental health variables
mh_vars <- my_data_testing %>%
  select(Anxiety, Depression, Insomnia, OCD) %>%
  drop_na()  # PCA requires complete cases

# Run PCA with scaling (important since variables are on same 0-10 scale,

# but scaling is still best practice)

pca_result <- prcomp(mh_vars, center = TRUE, scale. = TRUE)

# Summary: see how much variance each PC explains

summary(pca_result)

# Loadings: how each variable contributes to each PC
pca_result$rotation
# Scree plot — visualize variance explained by each component
screeplot(pca_result, type = "lines", main = "Scree Plot - Mental Health PCA")
abline(h = 1, col = "red", lty = 2)  # Kaiser criterion: keep PCs with eigenvalue > 1
```

### Screeplot for Principal Components in Mental Health Score

```{r}
#Formatted scree plot with variances
HIGHLIGHT <- "#e63946"
theme_ref <- theme_bw(base_family = "sans") +
  theme(
    plot.title       = element_text(face = "bold", size = 11),
    plot.subtitle    = element_text(size = 9, color = "grey40"),
    axis.text.x      = element_text(angle = 45, hjust = 1, size = 7),
    axis.text.y      = element_text(size = 8),
    panel.grid.minor = element_blank()
  )


total_variance <- sum(pca_result$sdev^2)
scree_df <- data.frame(
  PC         = paste0("PC", 1:min(4, length(pca_result$sdev))),
  eigenvalue = round(pca_result$sdev[1:min(4, length(pca_result$sdev))]^2, 3)
) %>%
  mutate(
    cumulative_pct = round(cumsum(eigenvalue) / total_variance * 100, 1),
    PC             = fct_inorder(PC)
  )

screeplot <- ggplot(scree_df, aes(x = PC)) +
  #Eigenvalue bars
  geom_col(aes(y = eigenvalue), fill = "#457b9d", width = 0.6) +
  geom_text(aes(y = eigenvalue, label = sprintf("%.2f", eigenvalue)),
            vjust = -0.5, size = 3) +
  #Cumulative variance line
  geom_line(aes(y = cumulative_pct * max(scree_df$eigenvalue) / 100,
                group = 1), color = HIGHLIGHT,
            linewidth = 1, linetype = "dashed") +
  geom_point(aes(y = cumulative_pct * max(scree_df$eigenvalue) / 100),
             color = HIGHLIGHT, size = 3) +
  geom_text(aes(y = cumulative_pct * max(scree_df$eigenvalue) / 100,
                label = sprintf("%.1f%%", cumulative_pct)),
            vjust = -0.8, hjust = 0.5, size = 2.8, color = HIGHLIGHT) +
  #Kaiser criterion line
  geom_hline(yintercept = 1, color = "red", linetype = "dotted",
             linewidth = 1) +
  annotate("text", x = Inf, y = 1.1, hjust = 1.1,
           label = "Kaiser criterion (lambda = 1)",
           color = "red", size = 3, fontface = "italic") +
  #Dual axes
  scale_y_continuous(
    name     = "Eigenvalue (lambda)",
    limits = c(0, max(scree_df$eigenvalue) * 1.15),
    sec.axis = sec_axis(
      transform = ~ . / max(scree_df$eigenvalue) * 100,
      name = "Cumulative Variance (%)",
      breaks    = seq(0, 100, by = 20),
      labels    = function(x) sprintf("%.0f%%", x)
    )
  ) +
  labs(
    title    = "Scree Plot for Mental Health Scores",
    subtitle = "Bars = eigenvalues (lambda) |\
    dashed line = cumulative variance |\
    dotted line = Kaiser criterion (lambda = 1)",
    x        = "Principal Component"
  ) +
  theme_ref +
  theme(
    axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 0, hjust = 0.5),
    #axis.title.y.right = element_text(color = HIGHLIGHT),
    axis.text.y.right  = element_text(color = HIGHLIGHT)
    )
screeplot
```

## Extract PC1 & PC2 scores for each person as the Mental Health Score

```{r}

# PC1 captures the most shared variance across all 4 conditions
# PC2 captures the contrast between conditions.
# For example high OCD/Anxiety vs low Insomnia/Depression or vice versa.

# Add PC1 scores back to the data (only for complete cases)
complete_idx <- complete.cases(my_data_testing %>% select(
  Anxiety, Depression, Insomnia, OCD))

# Add PC1 — general mental health burden (most shared variance)
my_data_testing$MentalHealthScore_PC1 <- NA
my_data_testing$MentalHealthScore_PC1[complete_idx] <- round(pca_result$x[, 1], 2)

# Add PC2 — secondary dimension (captures variance PC1 missed)
my_data_testing$MentalHealthScore_PC2 <- NA
my_data_testing$MentalHealthScore_PC2[complete_idx] <- round(pca_result$x[, 2], 2)

# Summary of both scores
summary(my_data_testing$MentalHealthScore_PC1)
summary(my_data_testing$MentalHealthScore_PC2)

# Hist plot — visualization of mental health scores
hist(my_data_testing$MentalHealthScore_PC1, 
     main = "Distribution of Mental Health Score (PC1)",
     xlab = "Mental Health Score", col = "steelblue")
hist(my_data_testing$MentalHealthScore_PC2, 
     main = "Distribution of Mental Health Score (PC2)",
     xlab = "Mental Health Score", col = "steelblue")
```

## Multiple Correspondence Analysis

```{r}
# Select genre variables
genre_vars <- my_data_testing %>%
  select(starts_with("Frequency_")) %>%
  mutate(across(everything(), as.factor))

# Create indicator matrix, each category becomes a 0/1 column
X <- model.matrix(~ . - 1, data = genre_vars)

# Apply Correspondence Analysis on matrix
ca_result <- ca(X)

# Plot full CA results
plot(ca_result, main = "Correspondence Analysis of Genre Preferences")

# Extract category coordinates
genre_coords <- as.data.frame(ca_result$colcoord)
genre_coords$category <- rownames(genre_coords)

# Clean category labels into genre names
# Removes "Frequency_" and the response levels
genre_coords$genre <- gsub(
  "Frequency_|Never|Rarely|Sometimes|Very frequently",
  "", genre_coords$category)
genre_coords$genre <- trimws(genre_coords$genre)

# Average coordinates per genre
# Gives one point per genre instead of one point per genre-response category
genre_avg <- genre_coords %>%
  group_by(genre) %>%
  summarise(
    Dim1 = mean(Dim1, na.rm = TRUE),
    Dim2 = mean(Dim2, na.rm = TRUE),
    Dim3 = mean(Dim3, na.rm = TRUE),
    Dim4 = mean(Dim4, na.rm = TRUE),
    Dim5 = mean(Dim5, na.rm = TRUE)
  )

# Compute distances between genres using the first 5 dimensions
dist_mat <- dist(genre_avg[, c("Dim1", "Dim2", "Dim3", "Dim4", "Dim5")])

# Perform hierarchical clustering
hc <- hclust(dist_mat, method = "ward.D2")

# Plot dendrogram
plot(hc, main = "Genre Clustering (Hierarchical)")

# Ran multiple tests with different k values (bc clustering was weak) 
# found that cutting the tree into 5 groups made the most sense
genre_avg$group <- cutree(hc, k = 5)

# Step 11: Final output
genre_final <- genre_avg %>%
  select(genre, group)

genre_final

# Step 12: Check group sizes
table(genre_final$group)

# Step 13: Add readable labels
genre_final$group_name <- case_when(
  genre_final$group == 1 ~ "Group 1",
  genre_final$group == 2 ~ "Group 2",
  genre_final$group == 3 ~ "Group 3",
  genre_final$group == 4 ~ "Group 4",
  genre_final$group == 5 ~ "Group 5"
  )

genre_final

# Make a clean plot with one point per genre,
# so it's much easier to interpret than the full CA plot
plot(genre_avg$Dim1, genre_avg$Dim2,
     col = genre_avg$group,
     pch = 19,
     xlab = "Dimension 1",
     ylab = "Dimension 2",
     main = "Genre Clusters (Clean View)")

text(genre_avg$Dim1, genre_avg$Dim2,
     labels = genre_avg$genre,
     pos = 3,
     cex = 0.8)

# Inspect genres by cluster
genre_final %>%
  arrange(group, genre)

# View genres grouped by cluster
genre_final %>%
  group_by(group) %>%
  summarise(genres = paste(genre, collapse = ", "))

split(genre_final$genre, genre_final$group)

# Convert frequency categories to numeric
freq_data <- my_data_testing %>%
  select(starts_with("Frequency_")) %>%
  mutate(across(everything(), ~ case_when(
    . == "Never" ~ 0,
    . == "Rarely" ~ 1,
    . == "Sometimes" ~ 2,
    . == "Very frequently" ~ 3,
    TRUE ~ NA_real_
  )))

# Map clustered genres to their frequency column names
genre_map <- genre_final %>%
  mutate(freq_col = paste0("Frequency_", genre))

# Compute average score per group for each person
group_scores <- sapply(sort(unique(genre_map$group)), function(g) {
  cols <- genre_map$freq_col[genre_map$group == g]
  cols <- cols[cols %in% names(freq_data)]
  
  rowMeans(freq_data[, cols, drop = FALSE], na.rm = TRUE)
})

# Assign each person to the group they listen to most
my_data_testing$GenreGroup <- apply(group_scores, 1, function(x) {
  if (all(is.na(x))) NA else which.max(x)
})

# Convert to factor
my_data_testing$GenreGroup <- as.factor(my_data_testing$GenreGroup)

# Check result
# my_data_testing
```

## Multiple Component Analysis Improved

```{r}
#Imporovements to Multiple Component Analysis

my_data_testing <- read.csv("data/my_data_testing.csv", header = TRUE)

# Select genre variables
mca_genre_vars <- my_data_testing %>%
  select(starts_with("Frequency_")) %>%
  mutate(across(everything(), as.factor))

# Run MCA
mca_result <- mjca(mca_genre_vars)
#summary(mca_result)

# Extract eigenvalues / % inertia explained
eig_vals <- mca_result$inertia.e  # or ca_result$sv^2 for raw ca()
pct_inertia <- eig_vals / sum(eig_vals) * 100
#cumsum(pct_inertia)

# Scree plot
# Only retain dimensions above the mean inertia line.
plot(pct_inertia, type = "b", 
     xlab = "Dimension", ylab = "% Inertia Explained",
     main = "Scree Plot — MCA Dimensions")
abline(h = mean(pct_inertia), col = "red", lty = 2)  # Kaiser-like rule

# Automatically select dimensions that lie above the mean inertia threshold.
n_dims <- (length(which(pct_inertia > mean(pct_inertia))))

#Modified Screeplot
mca_screedf <- data.frame(
  Dimension = seq_along(pct_inertia),
  Pct       = pct_inertia
)

#Plot Dimension contributions
ggplot(mca_screedf, aes(x = Dimension, y = Pct)) +
  geom_line(colour = "#4A90D9", linewidth = 0.8) +
  geom_point(
    aes(fill = Dimension <= n_dims),
    shape = 21, size = 3, colour = "white", stroke = 0.8
  ) +
  scale_fill_manual(
    name   = "",
    values = c("TRUE" = "#4A90D9", "FALSE" = "#AAAAAA"),
    labels = c("TRUE" = "Retained", "FALSE" = "Discarded"),
  ) +
  geom_hline(
    yintercept = mean(pct_inertia),
    linetype = "dashed", colour = "#E05C5C", linewidth = 0.7
  ) +
  annotate("text",
    x = max(mca_screedf$Dimension) * 0.75,
    y = mean(pct_inertia) + 1.5,
    label = sprintf("Mean inertia threshold (%.1f%%)", mean(pct_inertia)),
    colour = "#E05C5C", size = 3.2
  ) +
  labs(
    title    = "Scree Plot — MCA Dimensions",
    subtitle = sprintf(
      "Retaining %d dimension%s above mean inertia", n_dims,
      ifelse(n_dims == 1, "", "s")),
    x        = "Dimensions",
    y        = "% Inertia Explained"
  ) +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 13) +
  theme(
    plot.title    = element_text(face = "bold", hjust = 0.5),
    plot.subtitle = element_text(hjust = 0.5, colour = "grey40"),
    legend.position = "bottom",
    panel.grid.minor = element_blank()
  )


#Pair each expanded variable name with its corresponding level name
category_names <- paste(mca_result$levelnames, sep = ".")

# Extract Genre Coordinates
mca_genre_coords <- as.data.frame(mca_result$colcoord[, 1:n_dims])
colnames(mca_genre_coords) <- paste0("Dim", 1:n_dims)
mca_genre_coords$category <- category_names

# Split on the colon to get genre and response level as separate columns
mca_genre_coords <- mca_genre_coords %>%
  mutate(
    # Everything before the colon, minus the "Frequency_" prefix
    genre = gsub("^Frequency_", "", category) %>%
            gsub(":.*$", "", .),      # drop the colon and everything after it
    
    # Everything after the colon — the response level
    frequency = gsub("^.*:", "", category)
)

# Build a named lookup vector — category label maps to its mass.
# mca_result$levelnames gives names like "Frequency_Jazz:Never"
# mca_result$colmass gives the proportion of all responses that fell in each category
mass_lookup <- setNames(mca_result$colmass, mca_result$levelnames)

# Attach mass to your coords data frame by matching on the category column.
# This is safer than positional assignment (mca_genre_coords$mass <- col_masses)
# because it doesn't assume your rows are still in the original MCA order.
mca_genre_coords <- mca_genre_coords %>%
  mutate(mass = mass_lookup[category])


# Average per genre (centroid)
# Collapse the 4 response-level points per genre into one centroid
mca_genre_avg_weighted <- mca_genre_coords %>%
  group_by(genre) %>%
  summarise(across(starts_with("Dim"), mean, na.rm = TRUE))
                   #~ weighted.mean(.x, w = mass, na.rm = TRUE)))


# WEIGHTED CLUSTERING
# Weight each dimension by its share of variance
# so Dim1 (44%) has more pull than Dim3 (10%)
# Weight dimensions by variance when clustering
# This stops Dim5 having equal pull to Dim1 when computing distances
# Get % variance per dimension
pct_var <- eig_vals / sum(eig_vals)

# Scale coordinates by sqrt of variance explained before clustering
weighted_coords <- sweep(
  mca_genre_avg_weighted[, paste0("Dim", 1:n_dims)],
  MARGIN = 2,
  STATS = sqrt(pct_var[1:n_dims]),
  FUN = "*"
  )

# Attach genre names as row labels so the dendrogram is readable
rownames(weighted_coords) <- mca_genre_avg_weighted$genre
# Compute pairwise distances between genre centroids in the scaled space
dist_mat <- dist(weighted_coords)
# Ward's D2 minimises total within-cluster variance at each merge step,
# which tends to produce compact, evenly-sized clusters — well suited here
hc <- hclust(dist_mat, method = "ward.D2")
hc$labels

# Plot dendrogram
plot(hc, 
     main = "Genre Clustering (Variance-Weighted MCA Centroids)",
     xlab  = "Genre",
     ylab  = "Ward Linkage Distance",
     sub   = "")

# Use data-driven k selection instead of manual trial
# Pick the k with the highest silhouette width.
# Silhouette > 0.5 indicates strong structure;
# 0.25–0.5 is moderate. If all scores are low,
# it's a signal that the genres don't cluster cleanly
# and you may want to reconsider the approach entirely


# Silhouette analysis across multiple k values
sil_scores <- sapply(2:10, function(k) {
  cut <- cutree(hc, k = k)
  mean(silhouette(cut, dist_mat)[, 3])
})

best_k <- which.max(sil_scores) + 1

plot(2:10, sil_scores, type = "b",
     xlab = "Number of clusters (k)", ylab = "Mean Silhouette Width",
     main = "Silhouette Analysis for Optimal k")

# Confirmed k = 4 is optimal

k_range    <- 2:10
sil_scores <- sapply(k_range, function(k) {
  mean(silhouette(cutree(hc, k), dist_mat)[, 3])
})

sil_df <- data.frame(k = k_range, silhouette = sil_scores)

#plot of silhouette analysis
ggplot(sil_df, aes(x = k, y = silhouette)) +
  geom_line(colour = "#4A90D9", linewidth = 0.8) +
  geom_point(
    aes(fill = k == which.max(silhouette) + 1),
    shape = 21, size = 4, colour = "white", stroke = 0.8
  ) +
  scale_fill_manual(
    values = c("TRUE" = "#E05C5C", "FALSE" = "#4A90D9"), guide = "none") +
  annotate("text",
    x     = which.max(sil_scores) + 1,   # k = 3
    y     = max(sil_scores) + 0.008,
    label = paste0("Optimal k = ", which.max(sil_scores) + 1),
    colour = "#E05C5C", fontface = "bold", size = 3.5
  ) +
  scale_x_continuous(breaks = k_range) +
  labs(
    title    = "Silhouette Analysis for Optimal k",
    subtitle = "Higher mean silhouette width = more coherent clusters",
    x        = "Number of Clusters (k)",
    y        = "Mean Silhouette Width"
  ) +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 13) +
  theme(
    plot.title    = element_text(face = "bold", hjust = 0.5),
    plot.subtitle = element_text(hjust = 0.5, colour = "grey40"),
    panel.grid.minor = element_blank()
  )

#Set your preferred number of genre groups
best_k = 5
mca_genre_avg_weighted$group <- cutree(hc, k = best_k)

# Genre Groups: dynamically select columns from mca_genre_avg
mca_genre_final <- mca_genre_avg_weighted %>%
  select(genre, group, all_of(paste0("Dim", 1:n_dims)))

#Give groups meaningful names based on their genres
#Instead of "Group 1" through "Group 5"
mca_genre_final %>%
  arrange(group, genre) %>%
  group_by(group) %>%
  summarise(genres = paste(sort(genre), collapse = ", ")) %>%
  print()

# Then name groups based on what you see, e.g.:
mca_group_labels <- c(
  "1" = "Classical/Pop/Rock",
  "2" = "Country/Metal", 
  "3" = "Urban/Jazz",
  "4" = "Gospel",
  "5" = "Latin/Kpop"
#  "6" = "Pop",
#  "7" = "Rock"
)

mca_genre_final$group_name <- mca_group_labels[as.character(mca_genre_final$group)]

colour_pool <- c(
  "1" = "#4A90D9",   # Blue
  "2" = "#E05C5C",   # Red
  "3" = "#2ECC71",   # Green
  "4" = "orange",    # Orange
  "5" = "#9B59B6",   # Purple
  "6" = "pink",      # Amber
  "7" = "#b0bf1a",   # gray
  "8" = "gray"       # Teal
)

colour_palette <- setNames(
  colour_pool[1:best_k],
  as.character(1:best_k)
)

# cutree() returns a named vector where names are genre names
# (because we set rownames(weighted_coords) <- genre_avg$genre earlier in the pipeline).
# Subsetting by leaf_labels reorders it to match the dendrogram's display order.

leaf_labels <- hc$labels[order.dendrogram(as.dendrogram(hc))]
leaf_groups <- cutree(hc, k = best_k)[leaf_labels]

annotation_df <- data.frame(
  genre      = leaf_labels,
  x_pos      = seq_along(leaf_labels),
  group      = leaf_groups,
  group_name = mca_group_labels[as.character(leaf_groups)]
) %>%
  group_by(group, group_name) %>%
  summarise(
    # Midpoint x for the label text
    x_mid = mean(x_pos),
    # Min/max x with a small buffer for the shaded band behind the label
    x_min = min(x_pos) - 0.4,
    x_max = max(x_pos) + 0.4,
    .groups = "drop"
  ) %>%
  # Sort by x_mid (left-to-right position) NOT group number.
  # This is the key fix — everything downstream now reads clusters
  # in the same order that fviz_dend draws them left to right.
  arrange(x_mid)

# Derive the colour vector in left-to-right order by looking up each
# cluster's group number in the named palette.
# This single vector is used for BOTH fviz_dend AND annotate(),
# so the two are guaranteed to stay in sync.
ordered_colours <- colour_palette[as.character(annotation_df$group)]

#Set label y-position relative to the tree's actual height
y_label     <- -1
y_band_half <- 0.06 * max(hc$height)

fviz_dend(hc,
  k           = best_k,
  rect        = TRUE,
  rect_fill   = TRUE,
  horiz       = FALSE,          # Vertical layout — genre names land on x-axis
                                # where angle = 45 in the theme can rotate them
  rect_border = ordered_colours,
  k_colors    = ordered_colours,
  cex         = 0.75,
  lwd         = 0.6,
  main        = "Hierarchical Clustering of Music Genres",
  subtitle    = "Ward D2 linkage | Weighted MCA coordinates | k = 5",
  xlab        = "",
  ylab        = "Height (Ward D2 Distance)",
  ggtheme     = theme_minimal(base_size = 12)
) +
  # Shaded band — x maps to leaf positions, y maps to height (no flip confusion)
  annotate("rect",
    xmin  = annotation_df$x_min,
    xmax  = annotation_df$x_max,
    ymin  = y_label - y_band_half,
    ymax  = y_label + y_band_half,
    fill  = ordered_colours,
    alpha = 0.15
  ) +
  # Group name labels sit at the negative y offset, centred across each cluster
  annotate("text",
    x        = annotation_df$x_mid,
    y        = y_label,
    label    = annotation_df$group_name,
    colour   = ordered_colours,
    fontface = "bold.italic",
    size     = 4.5,
    angle    = 25,
    hjust    = 0.5,
    vjust    = 0.5
  ) +
  # Expand the y-axis (height axis) to create space below zero
  # where the group name labels now live
  scale_y_continuous(
    expand = expansion(mult = c(0)),
    limits = c(-1.25, NA)
    ) +
  coord_cartesian(clip = "off") +
  theme(
    plot.title    = element_text(face = "bold", hjust = 0.5),
    plot.subtitle = element_text(hjust = 0.5, colour = "grey40"),
    legend.position = "none"
    # 45-degree rotation — hjust = 1 right-aligns each label so it sits
    # neatly beneath its own tick mark rather than drifting sideways
    #axis.text.x   = element_text(angle = 45, hjust = 1, size = 9),
    # The large bottom margin is essential — angled labels occupy more
    # vertical space than straight ones and will be clipped without it
    #plot.margin   = margin(t = 10, r = 20, b = 90, l = 20)
  )

#CLUSTER SCATTER PLOT One point per genre, coloured and labelled by cluster

ggplot(mca_genre_final, aes(x = Dim1, y = Dim2,
                         colour = as.character(group),
                         label  = genre)) +
  geom_point(size = 3.5, alpha = 0.85) +
  geom_text_repel(
    size          = 3.2,
    max.overlaps  = 15,
    box.padding   = 0.4,
    point.padding = 0.3,
    segment.alpha = 0.4
  ) +
  stat_ellipse(
    aes(fill = as.character(group)),
    geom    = "polygon",
    alpha   = 0.08,
    level   = 0.75,
    show.legend = FALSE
  ) +
  scale_colour_manual(
    values = colour_palette,
    labels = mca_group_labels,
    name   = "Clusters:"
  ) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = colour_palette, guide = "none") +
  labs(
    title    = "Genre Clusters in MCA Space",
    subtitle = paste0(
      "Dimensions 1–4 retained | k = ", best_k,
      " clusters | Ward D2 linkage"
    ),
    x = paste0("Dimension 1 (", round(pct_inertia[1], 1), "% inertia)"),
    y = paste0("Dimension 2 (", round(pct_inertia[2], 1), "% inertia)")
  ) +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 13) +
  theme(
    plot.title      = element_text(face = "bold", hjust = 0.5),
    plot.subtitle   = element_text(hjust = 0.5, colour = "grey40"),
    legend.position = "bottom",
    panel.grid.minor = element_blank()
  )


#ASSIGN RESPONDENTS TO GENRE GROUPS

mca_freq_data <- my_data_testing %>%
  select(starts_with("Frequency_")) %>%
  mutate(across(everything(), ~ case_when(
    . == "Never"           ~ 0,
    . == "Rarely"          ~ 1,
    . == "Sometimes"       ~ 2,
    . == "Very frequently" ~ 3,
    TRUE                   ~ NA_real_
  )))

mca_genre_map <- mca_genre_final %>%
  mutate(freq_col = paste0("Frequency_", genre))

# For each cluster, compute the mean listening frequency per respondent
mca_group_scores <- sapply(sort(unique(mca_genre_map$group)), function(g) {
  cols <- mca_genre_map$freq_col[mca_genre_map$group == g]
  cols <- cols[cols %in% names(mca_freq_data)]
  rowMeans(mca_freq_data[, cols, drop = FALSE], na.rm = TRUE)
})

# Assign each person to their highest-scoring cluster
my_data_testing$GenreGroup <- apply(mca_group_scores, 1, function(x) {
  if (all(is.na(x))) NA else which.max(x)
})

my_data_testing$GenreGroup  <- as.factor(my_data_testing$GenreGroup)
my_data_testing$GenreGroup_name <- mca_group_labels[as.character(
  my_data_testing$GenreGroup)]

#RESPONDENT DISTRIBUTION PLOT
my_data_testing %>%
  filter(!is.na(GenreGroup)) %>%
  count(GenreGroup, GenreGroup_name) %>%
  ggplot(aes(x = reorder(GenreGroup_name, -n), y = n,
             fill = as.character(GenreGroup))) +
  geom_col(width = 0.6, alpha = 0.9) +
  geom_text(aes(label = n), vjust = -0.5, size = 3.5, fontface = "bold") +
  scale_fill_manual(values = colour_palette, guide = "none") +
  labs(
    title    = "Respondents per Genre Cluster",
    subtitle = "Based on highest mean listening frequency across cluster genres",
    x        = "Genre Cluster",
    y        = "Number of Respondents"
  ) +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 13) +
  theme(
    plot.title      = element_text(face = "bold", hjust = 0.5),
    plot.subtitle   = element_text(hjust = 0.5, colour = "grey40"),
    panel.grid.major.x = element_blank(),
    panel.grid.minor   = element_blank()
  )

#Merge Genre Frequencies with test data
my_data_testing_intermediate <- merge(
    my_data_testing, mca_freq_data, by = 0, all.x = TRUE
  ) |>
  mutate(Row.names = as.numeric(Row.names)) |>
  arrange(Row.names) |>
  select(-ends_with(".x")) |>
  rename_with(~ sub("\\.y$", "", .x))
```

## MCA Scatter Plot - Dimensions 1 vs 2 (Genre & Music Listening)

```{r}

# Build the plotting data frame using MCA row coordinates instead of PCA scores.
# mca_result$rowcoord contains one row per respondent and one column per dimension,
# directly analogous to pca_result$x — so the substitution is clean and direct.
pca_df <- as.data.frame(mca_result$rowcoord[, 1:2]) %>%
  rename(PC1 = V1, PC2 = V2) %>%    # Rename from default V1/V2 to PC1/PC2 so the
                                      # rest of the plotting code needs no changes
  mutate(
    hours       = my_data_testing$Hoursperday,
    genre_group = my_data_testing$GenreGroup_name,
    respondent  = row_number()
  )

# Extract MCA inertia percentages for the axis labels.
# mca_result$inertia.e gives raw inertia per dimension as a proportion of total,
# so multiplying by 100 converts to percentage — same arithmetic as the PCA version.
# If you want the Greenacre-adjusted values instead (which are more interpretable
# as discussed earlier), use mca_result$inertia.e.adjusted here instead.

mca_pct_inertia <- round(mca_result$inertia.e / sum(mca_result$inertia.e) * 100, 1)

genre_colours <- setNames(
  colour_palette,
  mca_group_labels[names(colour_palette)]
)


ggplot(pca_df, aes(x = PC1, y = PC2, color = genre_group)) +
  geom_hline(yintercept = 0,
             linetype = "dashed", colour = "black", linewidth = 0.5) +
  geom_vline(xintercept = 0,
             linetype = "dashed", colour = "black", linewidth = 0.5) +
  geom_point(aes(size = hours), alpha = 0.7) +
  scale_color_manual(
    values = genre_colours,
    name   = "Genre Group"
  ) +
  scale_size_continuous(
    name  = "Hours\nper Day",
    range = c(1.5, 6)
  ) +
  labs(
    title    = "MCA of Music Listening Patterns",
    subtitle = "Daily music listening time | coloured by genre group",
    # 'Inertia' replaces 'variance' since these are MCA dimensions, not PCA components.
    # The distinction matters if anyone reading the plot understands the methods
    # calling it variance in an MCA context would be technically incorrect.
    x = sprintf("Dim 1 (%.1f%% inertia)", mca_pct_inertia[1]),
    y = sprintf("Dim 2 (%.1f%% inertia)", mca_pct_inertia[2])
  ) +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 13) +
  theme(
    plot.title       = element_text(face = "bold", hjust = 0.5),
    plot.subtitle    = element_text(hjust = 0.5, colour = "grey40"),
    legend.position  = "right",
    panel.grid.minor = element_blank()
  )
```

## Modeling

### Load cleaned data

```{r}
my_data_testing_clean <- read.csv("data/my_data_testing_clean.csv", header = TRUE)
```

### Evaluate Simple Models

#### Mental Health Scores vs Music Listening Hours

```{r}
#Mental Health Scores vs Music Listening Hours
model1 <- lm(
  ConsolidatedMentalHealthScore_PC1 ~ HoursPerDay, data = my_data_testing_clean
  )

# View summaries/plots
summary(model1)
plot(model1, which = 1,
     labels.id = my_data_testing_clean$HoursPerDay)
bptest(model1)
model1_robustse <- sqrt(diag(vcovHC(model1, type="HC1")))

#Mental Health Scores vs Music Listening Hours
model2 <- lm(
  ConsolidatedMentalHealthScore_PC2 ~ HoursPerDay, data = my_data_testing_clean
  )

# View summaries/plots
summary(model2)
plot(model2, which = 1,
     labels.id = my_data_testing_clean$HoursPerDay)
model2_robustse <- sqrt(diag(vcovHC(model2, type="HC1")))
```

```{r, results='asis', warning=FALSE, message=FALSE}
stargazer(model1, model2,
          type="latex",
          se = list(model1_robustse, model2_robustse),
          star.cutoffs = c(0.05, 0.01, 0.001, NA),
          notes = "Significant at *p < 0.05, **p < 0.01, ***p < 0.001",
          title = "Regression Results for Mental Health Scores vs Listening Hours",
          dep.var.labels = c("Mental Health Score PC1", "Mental Health Score PC2"),
          covariate.labels = c("Hours per Day"),
          notes.append = FALSE,
          header = FALSE
          )
```

## Research Questions and Prep

**Does music genre have an impact on mental health?**

$X_i$ (independent variables): Genres

$Y_i$ (dependent variable): Mental health state (**total score/average** of Depression, Insomnia, OCD & Anxiety)

**Does time spent listening to music have an impact on mental health?**

$X_j$ (independent variable): Hoursperday

$Y_j$ (dependent variable): Mental health state

**How does tempo impact mental health?**

$X_k$ (independent variable): BPM

$Y_k$ (dependent variable): Mental health state

**Which genre results in the best sleep?**

$X_l$ (independent variable): genre

$Y_l$ (dependent variable): Insomnia

## Multivariate analysis

How do hours listened and genre impact mental health?

$Y = \beta_0 + \beta_1 X_i + \beta_2 X_j$

How do hours listened and tempo affect mental health states?

$Y = \beta_0 + \beta_1 X_j + \beta_2 X_k$

How do genre, listening time and tempo impact mental health?

$Y = \beta_0 + \beta_1 X_{i_1} + \beta_2 X_{i_2} + \cdots + \beta_k X_j + \beta_{k+1} X_k$

**Is there evidence of *overfitting* or *omitted-variable bias*?**

### Groupings

Should we group the mental health scores into a total? Should we group the types of music into fewer categories? Should we remove genres?

### Other Variables / Ideas

Hours per days - maybe omit less than 1s? People who like multi-genre vs single genre

### Research Questions

What is the appropriate ordinal test to do? Ordered logistic regression
